description: OVER-BROAD comment-stripping AND env-leak hole in the oracle. (a) test-deploy-akash.sh:8 strips comments with `sed 's/#.*//'`. This is NOT shell-aware: it will also blank out any legitimate `#` that appears inside a string literal, a parameter expansion default, or a heredoc line. In deploy-akash.sh the SDL heredoc and `${VAR:-default}` lines contain no `#`, so it is currently benign, but the technique is unsound and will silently corrupt INV grep results the moment a `#` appears in active code (e.g. a `${VAR:-#fff}` or a URL fragment). (b) The static `absent`/`have` greps run on the comment-stripped source, but the no-human INV-1 check `absent console-api|credit card|managed wallet` is the ONE check that SHOULD also scan comments (a smuggled console-api call hidden behind a comment-like `# console-api...` line followed by code would be stripped before the grep). The oracle strips comments for ALL checks uniformly.

evidence.snippet:
src="$(sed 's/#.*//' "$S")"   # strip comments
...
absent "console-api|credit card|managed wallet"  "INV-1 no-human"

correctFix: Use a shell-aware extractor or at minimum keep INV-1's no-human absent-check on the RAW file (so a console-api URL cannot hide). For the comment strip, prefer matching only full-line comments (`grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#'`) rather than `s/#.*//` which clobbers inline `#` in code.
